items.body: A coastal-modern Lake home with a separate guest house and three-well dock will be open for buyers to tour this Saturday in Gravois Mills. Stop by from 10 a.m.-2 p.m., or contact Jesse Faulstich at 573-260-0868 for more information.

items.title: After 40 Years, Clearwater Carpet Cleaning Joins U.S. Disaster Restoration
items.desc: After four decades serving Lake of the Ozarks, Clearwater Carpet Cleaning has transitioned ownership to an established local restoration company.
items.body: After four decades serving Lake of the Ozarks, Clearwater Carpet Cleaning has transitioned ownership to an established local restoration company. Clearwater Carpet Cleaning has been in business since 1986, when Cliff Bussey opened it with his partner Ron Conaway. "We opened on April 1st, so the joke would be on us if we didn't make it," Bussey said. His family had moved from northern Michigan, knowing almost no one. Using the radio, newspaper, and good ol' door knocking, Clearwater Carpet Cleaning became a dependable small business at the Lake. Work has been steady ever since. Over the years, Bussey and his team built a loyal customer base while handling everything from carpet, rug, upholstery, and air duct cleaning to flooring work and insurance-related fire and water restoration. Those services are still available, now with U.S. Disaster Restoration . Earlier this year, U.S. Disaster Restoration approached Bussey about purchasing Clearwater. He had already been considering selling for a couple of years, but he insisted on finding the right company to take over — especially with customers who had trusted him for decades. U.S. Disaster Restoration's team provides fast response and turnkey restoration services to help get properties back to normal — the kind of service Clearwater customers have come to expect. After 40 years in business, there are plenty of memorable jobs. One cleaning trip nearly ended with a truck in the Lake. Bussey recalled a company truck sliding down a gravel driveway during the winter, hitting a seawall, and somehow ending up balanced across it. With the Lake drawn down and rocks below, Bussey said another six inches could have sent the truck over the edge. items.title: New Lake Of The Ozarks Hotel Details Revealed: 126-Room Hyatt Planned In Backwater Jacks' Cove
items.desc: LAKE OF THE OZARKS, Mo. — A developer is looking to build a 126-room hotel under the Unscripted by Hyatt flag in Backwater Jacks' cove.
items.body: LAKE OF THE OZARKS, Mo. — A developer is looking to build a 126-room hotel under the Unscripted by Hyatt flag in Backwater Jacks' cove. The developer is Colorado-based Pedersen Development Company. The hotel, built on a 3.3-acre plot, would be called "The Cove Hotel." Unscripted by Hyatt is a line of upscale, independent, boutique hotels. Andy Prewitt, whose family owns and operates Backwater Jacks and the nearby LEVEL5 entertainment venue, confirmed his family is also involved with the hotel development. Prewitt said the rough timeline for construction is a 2027 build with a 2028 opening. The Osage Beach Board of Aldermen on Thursday evening, Oct. 15 will consider a resolution that would allow city staff to work with the developer on the project. The developer is not requesting real estate tax abatement, as has been done on some recent developments in the city. However, Pedersen is seeking Chapter 100 Industrial Revenue bonds as part of the funding. Chapter 100 Industrial bonds are a funding mechanism allowed under Missouri law that allow the city (in this case) to issue bonds that the developer would purchase. The funds from that purchase essentially flow through the city to the development, with the effect of allowing the developer an exemption on sales and use tax for some of the project construction materials. In the packet provided to the City Board of Aldermen, city staff provided the following explanation: "As part of the Chapter 100 bond transaction, the City and Developer will enter into a lease-leaseback transaction, and the City will issue industrial revenue bonds that are payable solely from lease payments made by the Developer. items.title: No, Patrick Mahomes Doesn't Have A Home At Lake Of The Ozarks. His Mom Says So.
items.body: "I wish[.] i love the lake." That's Patrick Mahomes' mom Randi Mahomes in her response to the social media fake stories that won't quit. And perhaps no celeb rumor makes its way through social media more often than the one that claims Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes has a Lake of the Ozarks home. A recent iteration occurred on the Instagram page of a St. Louis teacher, @michelle.in.stl, who posted a video of a well-known lakefront mansion (owned by a local businessman) with the overlaid text, "Patrick Mahomes lakehouse 📍Lake of the Ozarks Missouri." The caption read: "Sources claim this is Mahomes lakehouse." This is technically true... if your sources are other social media posts. She later added, "Update: sources are incorrect" Regardless of the facts, the video performed admirably, garnering 4.1 million views and 60k likes, to date. However, one of those 4.1 million views was from Patrick's mom. Kansas City Star sports writer Pete Grathoff found her in the comment section. "I wish i love the lake" she wrote simply. Let no one say investigative journalism is dead. Even if it only exists to debunk the same false claims about a celebrity... over and over. That said, if Mr. Mahomes would like to buy a house at the Lake, we've got a team that can help. Wish you had a Lake house? We can't get you next door to Mahomes (see above), but you can browse the entire lakefront market, at LakeExpoRealEstate.com .

items.title: Fall Harbor Hop Draws Nearly 2,300 Boaters For A Sunny Day At Lake Of The Ozarks
items.desc: LAKE OF THE OZARKS, Mo. – Boaters couldn't have asked for a better day on the water as the Lake celebrated the end of another fantastic season with the annual Fall Harbor Hop on Saturday, Oct.10.
items.body: LAKE OF THE OZARKS, Mo. – Boaters couldn't have asked for a better day on the water as the Lake celebrated the end of another fantastic season with the annual Fall Harbor Hop on Saturday, Oct.10. With beautiful weather and sunshine, the event welcomed 2,287 hoppers to wrap up the boating season with a poker run. The Harbor Hop is a popular tradition that brings boaters together for a day of fun, exploring the Lake and visiting participating waterfront restaurants and marinas. Participants travel along the Main Channel, Big Niangua Arm, and the Gravois Arm, collecting playing cards in hopes of building a winning hand and taking home prizes. "Having 2,287 hoppers participate is a great turnout, and shows just how much people love getting out on the water at the Lake," said Heather Brown, Executive Director of the Lake of the Ozarks Convention & Visitor Bureau. "One of the things that makes our destination so special is the ability to enjoy boating well into the fall. The Harbor Hop is a great opportunity to visit our incredible waterfront restaurants and marinas, enjoy the beautiful scenery, and celebrate everything that makes Lake of the Ozarks such a special destination." The two annual Harbor Hop events mark the beginning and end of boating season at the Lake. The Spring hop is typically held the first weekend of May to kick off summer, while the Fall hop takes place the second weekend of October to extend the season past Labor Day and showcase the beauty of autumn. The Lake of the Ozarks Convention & Visitor Bureau sponsors both events, with additional support from the Lake of the Ozarks Marine Dealers Association and participating waterfront restaurants and marinas. items.title: Free Philanthropy Workshop Open To Lake Area Professionals & Community Members
items.desc: LAKE OZARK, Mo. — The Community Foundation of the Lake and Community Foundation of the Ozarks are offering a free three-part virtual series focused on charitable giving, legacy planning, and philanthropy.
items.body: LAKE OZARK, Mo. — The Community Foundation of the Lake and Community Foundation of the Ozarks are offering a free three-part virtual series focused on charitable giving, legacy planning, and philanthropy. “Bringing Philanthropy Home to the Ozarks: A Participatory Workshop for Advisors” will be held from 10 to 11 a.m. Oct. 21, Oct. 28, and Nov. 4. The program is geared toward financial advisors, attorneys, CPAs, insurance agents, wealth strategists, and other professionals who help clients with financial, estate, and charitable-planning decisions. Nonprofit leaders, board members, donors, and other interested community members are also welcome to participate. National philanthropy educator Philip Cubeta will lead the series. Cubeta is the founder of Philanthropy Offerings and previously served for 12 years as the Wallace Chair in Philanthropy at The American College of Financial Services, where he oversaw the Chartered Advisor in Philanthropy designation program and taught legacy planning to more than 2,000 financial advisors and nonprofit gift planners. The first session will focus on the nonprofit and philanthropic landscape, including how charitable organizations are funded, challenges facing nonprofits, changing giving patterns, and the anticipated transfer of wealth between generations. The second session will center on values-based legacy planning and ways individuals and families can connect their financial resources with the people, places, institutions, and causes important to them. The final session will cover charitable-planning tools such as donor-advised funds, charitable remainder trusts, charitable gift annuities, private foundations, bequests, endowments, and gifts of appreciated or complex assets. items.title: When Temperatures Drop, Veteran-Owned Air-Exx HVAC Has Lake Homeowners' Backs
items.desc: When one Lake of the Ozarks homeowner’s air conditioner broke in the middle of summer, dealing with the heat just wasn’t an option. While waiting for a replacement part to arrive, Air-Exx HVAC owner Jay Napolitano went above and beyond…
items.body: When one Lake of the Ozarks homeowner’s air conditioner broke in the middle of summer, dealing with the heat just wasn’t an option. While waiting for a replacement part to arrive, Air-Exx HVAC owner Jay Napolitano went above and beyond to keep his client comfortable. He brought them a portable air conditioner. “It’s something a lot of companies don't offer,” Napolitano said. “We care about our clients. It's more than just a job to us.” Need an AC repair? Overdue for a tune-up? Give Air-Exx a call at 417-731-3027 or check out their Facebook page to get the ball rolling. That philosophy is at the heart of this veteran-owned HVAC company. For Napolitano, who served in the U.S. Army, that mindset of service didn't end when his military career did. “We were protecting our country,” Napolitano said. “Now I look at it like we're protecting your home.” That commitment was also evident when another client experienced a shattered blower wheel on an old system. The part was obsolete, and replacing it wasn't going to be the easiest route. But the only alternative was a complete system replacement that could easily run into thousands of dollars. Rather than immediately recommending an entirely new HVAC system, the company searched for — and found — a replacement part so the client could make the decision. “It was way less than a new system. We like to give clients the option if we can,” Napolitano explained. “We don't want to tell somebody they have to replace everything if there's another solution.” The company's approach is simple: diagnose the problem, explain the options and let the client make an informed decision. “We give options and solutions,” Napolitano said. And being local means understanding the unique needs of the Lake. So while PCE has specialized in commercial construction, the company has become an unexpected partner for an increasing number of Lake of the Ozarks condominium associations facing a growing problem: aging infrastructure. Rather than making quick repairs and moving on, PCE's team has been working with HOA boards and management companies to assess the condition of each building. That's allowed them to prioritize projects and develop repair plans that fit each association's budget and long-term goals. That consultative approach has earned praise from clients. items.title: Rockin’ Rogersville Grows Into Community Festival
items.desc: What started as a night of live music in Rogersville has grown into something quite a bit bigger. The ninth annual Rockin’ Rogersville brought music, food, local vendors and a […]
items.body: What started as a night of live music in Rogersville has grown into something quite a bit bigger. The ninth annual Rockin’ Rogersville brought music, food, local vendors and a new kids’ area together this year, all while raising money that will eventually make its way back into the community. The event is the signature fundraiser for the Community Foundation of Rogersville, an affiliate of the Community Foundation of the Ozarks. Christina Craig, board president of the Community Foundation of Rogersville, said the event has continued to change as organizers listen to what people want. “When it originally started, it was like a rock concert,” Craig said. The early version featured local bands, food trucks, and an evening fireworks show. This year looked a little different. Organizers added a vendor marketplace with 33 vendors, giving local artisans and crafters a chance to show and sell their work. Nine food trucks were also part of the event. A new kids’ zone helped move Rockin’ Rogersville even further toward becoming a full family festival. “We’re kind of trying to make it more of a family-centered event,” Craig said. “So not just a rock concert, but more of a festival.” Music is still a big part of it. Five bands performed this year, including KC and the Atta Boys, the Stephen James Gang, Dawson Hollow, Isaac Kenneth Band and KC Flo. Instead of sticking with one type of music, organizers mixed things up. Craig said previous years have leaned heavily toward either country or rock. This year’s lineup offered a little bluegrass, country, rockabilly, and rock. The foundation uses feedback from those attending to help decide what people would like to hear at future events. items.title: Lake Of The Ozarks Hit A New Heat Record On Tuesday
items.desc: LAKE OF THE OZARKS, Mo. — October felt like July on Tuesday, Oct. 13, at the Lake. The National Weather Service says temperatures reached into the low 90s — around 92 degrees by 2 p.m., with some areas reporting temps…
items.body: LAKE OF THE OZARKS, Mo. — October felt like July on Tuesday, Oct. 13, at the Lake. The National Weather Service says temperatures reached into the low 90s — around 92 degrees by 2 p.m., with some areas reporting temps as high as 94. The previous record for Oct. 13 was 90 degrees. Thankfully, after the sweltering heat, much-needed rain and cooler temps are on the horizon. The NWS says rain is likely Tuesday night through Thursday, with daytime temps landing in the mid-60s by the weekend.

items.title: Shine Through Faith Brings Helping Hands to Marshfield
items.desc: Sometimes, helping someone doesn’t take much. It might be mowing a yard, picking up groceries, or simply making sure an elderly neighbor has someone to turn to. That’s the idea […]
items.body: Sometimes, helping someone doesn’t take much. It might be mowing a yard, picking up groceries, or simply making sure an elderly neighbor has someone to turn to. That’s the idea behind Shine Through Faith, a Marshfield nonprofit founded by Heather Rodriguez. What started as a way to help older residents remain in their homes has grown into a community resource center helping families, foster children, teachers, and others who need a hand. For Rodriguez, the organization grew out of some difficult times in her own life. She has spent much of her life between Missouri and Arizona. Her grandparents lived in Missouri, and she raised her daughters here for much of their childhood. After spending more time in Arizona, she and her family returned to Missouri so their younger boys could grow up here, too. Rodriguez has always enjoyed volunteering and helping others. But after being diagnosed with thyroid cancer and having to medically retire, she found herself wondering what came next. “I thought everything was over,” she said. During that time, Rodriguez said she felt God leading her toward something called Shine Through Faith. She just wasn’t sure what it was supposed to become. About five years later, after meeting several elderly people who had little or no family support, the answer began to take shape. “I was like, how can I make a difference with them?” she said. That question became the starting point for Shine Through Faith. The original mission was simple: help elderly residents stay in their own homes longer by connecting them with volunteers who could handle everyday tasks.
